elements.element: No minimum purchase commitment imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer commits to purchase no minimum amount of Services"

elements.element: Fees payable only for usage or ordered Services
elements.evidence: "pays only for Services ordered or used"

elements.element: No take-or-pay obligation / no volume restriction on Customer
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term
elements.evidence: clause still refers to "each of the next three years"; no 12-month limitation
no notice-based reduction mechanic appears in the revised clause

elements.element: True-up rather than penalty for shortfall
elements.evidence: no true-up mechanic; take-or-pay simply deleted

reasons: Locked target is preferred, and the redline delivers both preferred atomic elements: no minimum commitment and fees only for Services ordered or used.

The residual trailing words were converted from "without reduction or termination rights" to "without take-or-pay, reduction or termination restrictions," which removes the harmful no-exit language rather than adding new free-standing rights; no undefined terms or dangling mechanics are introduced.

Fallback elements (12-month limit, 30 days' notice reduction, true-up) are absent, but that is irrelevant because the separate preferred bargain is complete; the margin comment appropriately offers the fallback for negotiation.
Drafting nit only: "commits to purchase no minimum amount" reads awkwardly; a cleaner formulation would be "Customer has no minimum purchase commitment," but the operative effect is unambiguous.
